rulings.reason: The instruction makes the judge read the content and determine whether it engages the rule's provisions on the merits at all, so a high score is direct (negatively signed) evidence about substantive engagement rather than about length, format, or provenance. The proposer's timing-pressure parent tag is not what the text actually asks a judge to detect.

The criterion scores where in the document the ask appears, not whether the ask is supported, so a substantively empty comment can score 10 -- indeed the proposer's own exemplar R08 is a bare extension request. Front-loading is a drafting convention that fingerprints trained regulatory-affairs authors, who plausibly also write genuinely stronger comments, hence mixed.

Membership counts, statutory mandate, and years of operation are assertions about who is speaking and with what resources, not argument about the rule, which is precisely an upstream-circumstance fingerprint. Well-resourced organizations with real standing often do submit substantively better comments, so the channel is mixed rather than purely spurious.
